title: Fit to Drive: Alcohol, Drugs & Tiredness
whatItIs: You must be fit to drive: report health conditions to DVLA, meet the eyesight rule, and never drive over the alcohol or drug limits. Don't start a journey tired.

keyFacts.text: You MUST report to DVLA any health condition likely to affect your driving.
You MUST be able to read a number plate from 20 metres in good daylight, with glasses if you need them.
England and Wales: you MUST NOT drive above 35 µg of alcohol per 100 ml of breath (80 mg per 100 ml of blood).

keyFacts: Alcohol takes time to leave your body: you may be unfit to drive the next morning.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT drive under the influence of drugs or medicine. Check with your doctor or pharmacist.

keyFacts: Don't begin a journey tired. Avoid long journeys between midnight and 6 am, when alertness is lowest.

a.label: Highway Code advice (all drivers)
points: A break of at least 15 minutes after every 2 hours of driving

b.label: Drivers' hours law (lorries)
points: A break of at least 45 minutes after no more than 4.5 hours of driving
A legal requirement under the assimilated rules

onTheTest.question: You are driving a lorry in Scotland. What is the legal limit for alcohol in your breath?
onTheTest.why: In Scotland you MUST NOT drive with a breath alcohol level higher than 22 microgrammes per 100 ml of breath. In England and Wales the limit is 35.

onTheTest.question: You start to feel sleepy while driving on a motorway. What should you do?
options: Stop on the hard shoulder for a short sleep
Stop at a service area or leave at the next exit
Turn up the radio and keep going
onTheTest.why: Rule 91: stop in a safe place, not in an emergency area or on the hard shoulder. Rule 262: use service areas or facilities off motorway exits.

traps: Below the limit is not the same as safe: any alcohol reduces your driving ability.
Prescribed medicines can impair you too.
Illegal drug limits are very low: even a small amount can put you over.
Scotland has lower drink-drive limits than England and Wales.
